title: Inference backend selector and per-model micro-tuning manifest for heterogenous MHA/GQA/MoE
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We need a deterministic, observable mechanism that selects an optimized inference backend and compilation tuning profile when a new model variant (MHA/GQA/MoE) is onboarded or during runtime model substitution. Current onboarding pins are ad-hoc and split across build metadata, causing regressions and manual rollbacks. This ticket defines an "inference backend selector" plus a human-editable per-model micro-tuning manifest that encodes kernel choices, compile flags, quantization profile, and safe fallback chains. Goal: reduce time-to-safe-onboard by 50% for complex architectures and enable automated publishing of performance profiles to the catalog.
acceptance_criteria: A stable manifest schema (v1) exists and is stored with model version metadata in the model catalog
Runtime can atomically resolve a model->backend selection using the manifest and return deterministic kernel set and compile flags
Onboard flow produces a published performance profile and telemetry that matches expected targets within +/-10% for latency and throughput on test Harness
Pinning API allows operators to mark a manifest as 'active' and supports rollback to previous manifest versions
Documentation and example manifests for an MHA, a GQA variant, and a 64-expert MoE are added to the onboarding guide
design_summary: Introduce two pieces: 1) a lightweight selector service that accepts a model signature (arch, hidden_size, seq_len_dist, gating_density, num_experts, shard_count, quantizable) and returns a backend candidate list ordered by preference; 2) a per-model micro-tuning manifest authored by Runtime/Onboarder containing: kernel_set, compile_flags, quant_profile_name, kv_cache_mode, recommended_batching/windowing hints, and fallback candidates. Selector uses selector rules (static) + runtime telemetry scoring (learned weights) to order candidates. Manifests are versioned, signed, and published to the model catalog with immutable history and an 'active' pointer.
manifest_schema_snippet: schema_v1: fields= [ 'model_key', 'manifest_version', 'created_by', 'arch_tags', 'sequence_profiles', 'kernel_set', 'compile_flags', 'quant_profile', 'kv_cache_hint', 'batching_hints', 'fallback_chain', 'safety_checks', 'perf_targets' ] - example values: arch_tags=[MHA, GQA], kernel_set=['attention_fused','fast_matmul_v2'], compile_flags=['fast_gelu=true','use_tensorcores=auto'], quant_profile='q4_0_dynamic', fallback_chain=['kernel_v1','kernel_scalar']
implementation_notes: Add a manifest store table to model-catalog (immutable objects + pointer to active manifest).
Selector service: gRPC endpoint selector.Resolve(model_signature) -> ordered candidates; local cache in runtime agents for <500ms lookup.

Runtime agent consumes resolved kernel_set and tries to load kernels in order; on failure uses fallback_chain. Failures are non-fatal but emit SEARCH_FAIL telemetry and increment manifest safety counter.
Add API endpoints: POST /models/:id/manifests (create), POST /models/:id/manifests/:v/activate, GET /models/:id/manifests/:v, GET /models/:id/manifests/active
Schema validation must include explicit safety_checks: required ops, maximum memory budget, supported quant modes. Reject manifest publish if safety_checks fail on a canonical test runner.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Implement manifest store + selector service behind a feature flag; onboard three internal models (mha-base, gqa-4b, moe-64e) using authored manifests; route 1% traffic for each to selector-backed runtime agents
Phase 2 (expanded canary): Increase to 10% traffic and run full perf/e2e tests with CI harness; validate rollback path; monitor perf targets and safety counters
Phase 3 (default): Flip feature flag for Dedicated/Hosted runtime; enable manifest activation UI in Console; publish onboarding docs
Rollback: activation API must allow immediate revert to previous active manifest and runtime agents must pick up revert within 30s
testing_plan: Unit: manifest schema validation, selector rule unit tests, negative manifests test
Integration: full creation->activate->runtime-resolve flow using model-catalog staging and runtime agent (CI job).
Perf: run canonical harness for each architecture and assert latency P50/P95 and throughput vs baseline (baseline = current pinned profile)
Safety: run 'manifest safety runner' that validates memory footprint and mandatory kernel op presence for worst-case sequence lengths
Chaos: craft failure cases where top kernel fails to load and ensure fallback_chain works and metrics emitted
telemetry_metrics: manifest.activate.count - increment when an activation call succeeds
manifest.rollback.count - increment when activation rolls back
manifest.safety_failures - counter for published manifests that fail safety runner
perf.delta.p95 - measured delta against baseline for P95 latency after activation
risks: Incorrect manifest could cause widespread perf regressions if activated without canary. Mitigation: safety_runner + staged rollout.
Selector rules become stale as new kernels and quant profiles are added. Mitigation: automated weekly telemetry-based reweighting and a dashboard for rule drift.
Operational complexity for Dedicated customers who pin kernels manually. Mitigation: provide 'snapshot manifest' export for Dedicated and a controlled import process.
API contention if many models activate manifests simultaneously. Mitigation: rate-limit activations and provide async activation status.
